newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Highlights of Friday's Commission briefing.
newsitem.headline: Highlights of Friday's Commission briefing.

text.p: Following are highlights of the midday briefing by the European Commission on Friday:
Spokesman Nikolaus van der Pas said the Commission would hold its weekly meeting on Thursday in Brussels instead of Wednesday.

Spokeswoman Heike Gerstbrein said Commissioner Monika Wulf-Mathies had sent a letter to Belgian Walloon Government President Robert Collignon to tell him how structural funds could help the Walloon Region face the consequences of Forges de Clabecq's financial problems. Gerstbrein said one of the possibilities would be to add the towns of Tubize and Rebecq to the Objective 2 programme's list.

In answer to a question, spokesman Jean-Christophe Filori said Commissioner Neil Kinnock maintained that airport slot-sellings were not allowed. Spokesman Willy Helin said Commissioner Karel Van Miert agreed with this point of view.

Regarding recent events involving trade union rights in South Korea, spokesman Peter Guilford said the human rights clause included in the EU/South-Korean framework agreement could not be invoked since this agreement had not been ratified yet and it was not clear whether human rights covered labour rights.

Spokesman Nicolaas Wegter said the agenda of the meeting gathering Commissioners Sir Leon Brittan, Hans van den Broek and Karel Van Miert with Japanese Minister of International Trade and Industry Shinji Sato would include the Information Technology Agreement, telecoms and EU/Japan trade disputes.

Asked to react to France's refusal to allow U.S. genetically-modified maize on the market, spokesman Peter Jorgensen said that until the Commission's December decision on genetically modified organisms was implemented, it remained illegal to import the maize or to put it on the market.
The Commission released the following documents:
- IP/97/10: Angola: Commission approves humanitarian aid to plan worth ECU 14 million.
- European Commission and the World Bank: Bosnia reconstruction priorities agreed for 1997.
- Speech by Christine Wallich, country director, Bosnia-Herzegovina, the World Bank, at the donors information conference.
- Memo/97/3: Calendar of the Commission's activities during the week of January 13-17, 1997.
